title: Stop a leaking pipe with a hinged repair clamp: set it over the split, squeeze its halves shut until it latches
instruction: Clamp the leak on this pipe with the repair clamp.
context: Clamping a split pipe until it can be replaced is routine emergency work for plumbers and building maintenance workers (O*NET 47-2152.00 Plumbers, Pipefitters, and Steamfitters; 49-9071.00 Maintenance and Repair Workers, General; about 2 million US workers together, BLS OEWS May 2024). The clamp must be centred on the split so its lining covers it, set over the pipe, and squeezed shut round it until it latches.
setup: Millimetres; x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the robot's left, z above the table top; arm bases at y +305 and -305. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot. (1) A plumbing training board on the bench at x 320, and on it a 3/4 in copper pipe (22.2 mm outside) along y from y -170 to 170, its axis 75 mm up, on two steel stands at y -150 and 150. A 20 mm red band round the pipe at y -40 marks its split. (2) A 75 mm hinged pipe repair clamp, 80 g: two lined steel half shells with a 25.2 mm bore, hinged together along the top with a 10 mm knuckle, each with a rubber grip pad on its outer face and a latch lug on its lower edge; a spring holds the halves 28 degrees open. It stands open on its feet on the bench at x 200, y -200, its bore along y.
scoring: Measured at the end of the trial. 1.0 (success, must hold for 1 s) when the clamp is latched shut round the pipe (both halves squeezed to within 2 degrees of shut with its bore on the pipe: its axis within 4 mm of the pipe's and lined up within 10 degrees) and centred over the leak (its middle within 12 mm of the red band's), both grippers 30 mm or more from it and nothing moving more than 1 mm for 1 s; 0.75 when it is latched over the leak but a gripper is near or it still moves; 0.5 when it is latched round the pipe but not over the leak; 0.25 when the clamp sat on the pipe over the leak at some point; else 0.
reset_notes: Press the latch to release the clamp, take it off the pipe and stand it open on its feet at its mark, bore along the pipe.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at true size; the pipe is an exact mesh, the clamp's half shells are steel staves hinged on a pin. The halves' opening spring and the snap latch are drives on the hinges: free under the spring until both are squeezed to within 2 degrees of shut round the pipe, then held shut. The rubber lining's seal and the water are not simulated. All geometry is generated by code in the package.
